messages.text: Zverev books place in ATP Finals semi-finals

metadata.summary: Alexander Zverev booked his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals after sealing a ruthless 6-2 7-6 (7-4) victory over Ben Shelton in Turin on Tuesday night, in a rematch of this year's US Open final.
metadata.content: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in straight sets to book his place in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals; Rafael Jodar will not progress past the groups after he suffered defeat to Arthur Fils; watch the ATP Nitto Finals live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 17 November 2026 22:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev booked his spot in knockout stages of the ATP Finals with a victory against Ben Shelton Alexander Zverev booked his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals after sealing a ruthless 6-2 7-6 (7-4) victory over Ben Shelton in Turin on Tuesday night, in a rematch of this year's US Open final. His victory means debutant Rafael Jodar will not advance to the semi-finals after the Spaniard suffered defeat to Zverev in their opening match of the tournament, before being bested 4-6 6-2 6-2 by Arthur Fils earlier in the day. Zverev, whose service game was impeccable against Shelton, will jump to the top of the John McEnroe Group standings, having not dropped a set so far during the tournament, as he swept away the American to bring up a flawless 7-0 winning record against the 24-year-old. metadata.summary: Nico de Boinville was given security support at Plumpton on Monday after a threat against the jockey was received and passed on to authorities.
metadata.content: Nico de Boinville 'escorted to his vehicle' and given security support after threat received | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nico de Boinville 'escorted to his vehicle' and given security support after threat received Top jockey Nico de Boinville was racing at Plumpton and finished fifth in the opening race of the afternoon, before finishing third on his only other ride; he was given additional security protection throughout the day after a threat had been made to Nicky Henderson's yard Tuesday 17 November 2026 19:16, UK Image: Nico de Boinville was given additional security at Plumpton on Monday Nico de Boinville was given security support at Plumpton on Monday after a threat against the jockey was received and passed on to authorities. The multiple Grade One-wining jockey finished fifth aboard even-money favourite Ginolo for his boss Nicky Henderson in the opening race of the afternoon at the East Sussex track, after which he was informed he would be provided with extra security after officials became aware of the situation. De Boinville went on to finish third on his only other ride, the Henderson-trained Ionian in a handicap chase, the third race on the card. Explaining the sequence of events, Plumpton's clerk of the course Marcus Waters said: "We got a phone call from a person representing the PJA (Professional Jockeys Association) and the NTF (National Trainers Federation) regarding a threat that had gone in to the Henderson yard. The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home. Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life. "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone.
